# Acceleration techniques

The time complexity scales as 

$$
T \propto n_{\text{live}} \times \langle t_{\text{like}} \rangle \times \langle n_{\text{replace}}\rangle \times  D_{\pi}  
$$

where

- $n_\text{live}$ is the number of live points used
- $\langle t_{\text{like}} \rangle$ is the average likelihood evaluation time
- $\langle n_\text{replace} \rangle$ is the average number of likelihood evaluations required to find a replacement
- $D_{\pi} = KL(p \parallel \pi)$ is the KL divergence between posterior and prior, i.e. the volumetric compression between the posterior typical region and the prior

Based on this equation, we can directly think of several ways to accelerate sampling [@rouletInferringBinaryProperties2024].
